pool.text:
Let \( h(x) = \displaystyle\int_0^x f(t)\,dt \) where \( f \) is piecewise linear with \( f(0)=0, f(2)=4, f(4)=0, f(6)=-2 \).
(a) Find \( h(4) \).
(b) Where does \( h \) attain a local maximum on \((0,6)\)?
pool.sol:
(a) \( h(4) = \frac{1}{2}(4)(4)=8 \).
(b) \( h'(x)=f(x) \) changes from positive to negative at \( x=4 \), so local max at \( x=4 \).

pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} 2x^2\,dx = \frac{2}{3}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{1}^{2} 2x^2\,dx = \frac{14}{3}\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2} 2x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{2} = \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} + \displaystyle\int_{1}^{2} = \frac{2}{3} + \frac{14}{3} = \frac{16}{3}\).

pool.domain: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} 2x^2\,dx = 18\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3} 2x^2\,dx = 18\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3} 2x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3} = \displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{3} = 18 + 18 = 36\).

pool.domain: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} 1x^2\,dx = 9\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{3} 1x^2\,dx = 9\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3} 1x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{3} = \displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{3} = 9 + 9 = 18\).

pool.domain: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{-2} 2x^2\,dx = \frac{38}{3}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0} 2x^2\,dx = \frac{16}{3}\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} 2x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{0} = \displaystyle\int_{-3}^{-2} + \displaystyle\int_{-2}^{0} = \frac{38}{3} + \frac{16}{3} = 18\).

pool.domain: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{-1} 3x^2\,dx = 26\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} 3x^2\,dx = 9\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{2} 3x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{-3}^{2} = \displaystyle\int_{-3}^{-1} + \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{2} = 26 + 9 = 35\).

pool.domain: Unit 6 · Integration and Accumulation of Change
pool.text: Given \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} 4x^2\,dx = \frac{4}{3}\) and \(\displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} 4x^2\,dx = \frac{4}{3}\), find \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} 4x^2\,dx\).
pool.sol: By additivity of the definite integral: \(\displaystyle\int_{-1}^{1} = \displaystyle\int_{-1}^{0} + \displaystyle\int_{0}^{1} = \frac{4}{3} + \frac{4}{3} = \frac{8}{3}\).

(a) \[ \frac{dy}{y} = 2x\,dx \Rightarrow \ln|y| = x^2 + C \Rightarrow y = Ae^{x^2} \]
\( y(0)=3 \Rightarrow A=3 \), so \( y = 3e^{x^2} \).
(b) \( y(1) = 3e \)
